tasks.title: Set up Supabase database schema with PostGIS extension
tasks.description: Create all required database tables (lighting_points, incidents, overlast_zones, unsafe_areas, buurt_baseline, safety_grid) with PostGIS geometry support
tasks.details:
1. Enable PostGIS extension in Supabase
2. Create tables matching PRD schema:
   - lighting_points: id (uuid), lat (float), lng (float), type (text), imported_at (timestamp)
   - incidents: id (uuid), lat (float), lng (float), category (text), occurred_at (timestamp), imported_at (timestamp)
   - overlast_zones: id (uuid), kind (text), geometry (jsonb), validity_days (text[]), validity_hours (text), polarity (text)
   - unsafe_areas: id (uuid), name (text), kind (text), source (text), geometry (jsonb)
   - buurt_baseline: buurt_code (text, PK), veiligheidsindex (float), updated_at (timestamp)
   - safety_grid: id (uuid), grid_x (int), grid_y (int), lat (float), lng (float), buurt_code (text), lighting_score (float), incident_score (float), building_density_score (float), overview_score (float), camera_bonus (float), overlast_penalty (float), hotspot_penalty (float), updated_at (timestamp)
3. Add indexes on lat/lng columns and grid_x/grid_y for query performance
4. Create Supabase migration file using `supabase migration new initial_schema`
tasks.testStrategy: Verify all tables exist with correct schema using Supabase dashboard or psql. Run test INSERT/SELECT queries. Confirm PostGIS extension is enabled by running SELECT PostGIS_Version().

tasks.title: Create data import pipeline for Amsterdam Data API layers
tasks.description: Build Python ETL scripts to fetch and import street lighting, incidents, overlast zones, BAG building data, and neighborhood boundaries from Amsterdam Data API into Supabase
tasks.details:
1. Get Amsterdam Data API key from https://keys.api.data.amsterdam.nl/clients/v1/ and add to backend/.env as AMSTERDAM_DATA_API_KEY
2. Create backend/data_import/ directory with separate scripts:
   - import_lighting.py: fetch /v1/leidingeninfrastructuur/amsterdam_ovl_lichtpunten, parse coords, insert into lighting_points
   - import_incidents.py: fetch /v1/meldingen (SIA), filter to person/group/public-space categories from last 24 months, geocode, insert into incidents
   - import_overlast_zones.py: fetch /v1/overlastgebieden, parse 16 zone types with time validity, store geometry as GeoJSON in jsonb, mark cameratoezicht as bonus polarity
   - import_bag.py: fetch /v1/bag, aggregate building density per ~100m grid cell
   - import_gebieden.py: fetch /v1/gebieden for buurt polygons
3. Use httpx for async API calls with retry logic
4. Implement pagination handling for large datasets
5. Add logging and error handling
6. Create CLI script backend/import_all.py that runs all imports sequentially
tasks.testStrategy: Run each import script individually and verify data appears in Supabase tables. Check row counts match expected data volume. Validate geometry/jsonb fields parse correctly. Run import_all.py and confirm all tables populated.

tasks.title: Import Veiligheidsindex 2025-3 baseline and survey unsafe areas
tasks.description: Parse and import neighborhood safety baseline scores from XLSX and geocode unsafe areas from the 2025 cyclist survey into Supabase
tasks.details:
1. Download Veiligheidsindex 2025-3 XLSX from https://onderzoek.amsterdam.nl/dataset/openbare-orde-en-veiligheid
2. Create backend/data_import/import_veiligheidsindex.py:
   - Use openpyxl or pandas to parse XLSX
   - Extract buurt_code and composite veiligheidsindex score
   - Normalize scores to 0.0-1.0 range
   - INSERT into buurt_baseline table
3. Create backend/data_import/import_unsafe_areas.py:
   - Manually geocode the 22 clusters + 8 parks + 8 corridors from survey Table 1
   - Geocode §1.7 hard-to-avoid corridors (Gooiseweg, Diemerpark, etc.)
   - Geocode §1.8 specific locations (Vondelpark, Leidseplein, stations, etc.)
   - For parks, use Amsterdam Data API /v1/functionele_gebieden to get exact polygons
   - For corridors/clusters, create approximate polygon or linestring geometries
   - Tag each with appropriate kind (park/square/station/corridor/cluster) and source (survey_cluster/survey_corridor/survey_hotspot_type)
   - INSERT into unsafe_areas table
4. Store geometries as GeoJSON in jsonb column
tasks.testStrategy: Verify buurt_baseline has entries for all Amsterdam buurten with scores 0.0-1.0. Confirm unsafe_areas table has entries for all survey locations with valid GeoJSON geometry. Spot-check a few well-known areas (Vondelpark, Leidseplein) have correct coordinates.

tasks.title: Implement pre-computed safety_grid scoring engine
tasks.description: Build grid generation and static layer scoring system that computes lighting, incident, building density, overview, camera, overlast, and hotspot scores per ~100m cell
tasks.details:
1. Create backend/grid_scorer.py module
2. Implement grid generation:
   - Cover Amsterdam bbox (52.278, 4.728 to 52.431, 5.079) with ~100m cells
   - Use Haversine formula or simple lat/lng arithmetic
   - Store grid_x, grid_y, center lat/lng
3. Implement per-cell scoring functions:
   - lighting_score: density of lichtpunten within cell radius → 0.0-1.0
   - incident_score: inverted density of meldingen (last 24m) → 0.0-1.0 (fewer = higher)
   - building_density_score: BAG residential + non-residential count → 0.0-1.0
   - overview_score: inverse of dense-green coverage (parks/tunnels) → 0.0-1.0
   - camera_bonus: 0.0-0.2 if cell overlaps cameratoezicht zone
   - overlast_penalty: 0.0-0.3 if cell overlaps active overlastgebieden (time-valid)
   - hotspot_penalty: 0.0-0.2 if cell intersects unsafe_areas
4. Join to buurt_code via gebieden polygons
5. Batch INSERT/UPDATE into safety_grid table
6. Create CLI script backend/compute_grid.py to regenerate grid
tasks.testStrategy: Run compute_grid.py and verify safety_grid table populated. Spot-check a few cells in known safe areas (residential neighborhoods) have high scores. Check cells in known unsafe areas (survey hotspots) have lower scores. Verify all subscores are in valid ranges.

tasks.title: Implement time-aware people density scoring with crowdmonitor fallback
tasks.description: Build dynamic people-density scoring using Amsterdam crowdmonitor sensor data with time-of-day heuristic fallback for areas without coverage
tasks.details:
1. Create backend/people_density.py module
2. Implement crowdmonitor integration:
   - Fetch real-time data from Amsterdam Data API /v1/crowdmonitor
   - Map sensor readings to grid cells
   - Cache results for 15 min to reduce API calls
3. Implement heuristic fallback for uncovered areas:
   - Define time windows: day (06-20), evening (20-23), night (23-06)
   - Define street types: residential, commercial, park, transit
   - Create lookup table: street_type × time_window → density estimate (0.0-1.0)
   - Use building_density_score and unsafe_area kind to infer street type
4. Create function get_people_density(lat, lng, time) that:
   - Checks crowdmonitor cache first
   - Falls back to heuristic if no sensor coverage
   - Returns 0.0-1.0 score
5. Add UI flag to indicate when heuristic is used vs real sensor data
tasks.testStrategy: Test with various lat/lng/time combinations. Verify crowdmonitor data is used when available. Confirm heuristic returns sensible values for uncovered areas. Check that residential areas at night get low density scores, commercial areas during day get high scores.

tasks.title: Build deterministic route scoring and selection engine
tasks.description: Implement the weighted safety scoring formula with time-of-day layer weights and route selection logic that picks the highest-scoring alternative from Google Directions
tasks.details:
1. Create backend/route_scorer.py module
2. Implement time-of-day weight tables from PRD Table (survey-seeded):
   - Day (06-20): people 0.22, overview 0.16, lighting 0.14, buildings 0.18, camera 0.04, overlast -0.08, incidents -0.10, hotspot -0.08
   - Evening (20-23): people 0.20, overview 0.18, lighting 0.20, buildings 0.14, camera 0.06, overlast -0.14, incidents -0.10, hotspot -0.12
   - Night (23-06): people 0.18, overview 0.20, lighting 0.26, buildings 0.10, camera 0.08, overlast -0.18, incidents -0.10, hotspot -0.16
3. Implement cell_score(lat, lng, time) function
4. Implement route_score(polyline, time) function
5. Implement select_safest_route(alternatives, time)
tasks.testStrategy: Create test routes through known safe vs unsafe areas. Verify scoring returns expected ordering. Test time-of-day changes affect scores correctly. Confirm route selection picks the expected alternative.

tasks.title: Integrate Anthropic Claude SDK for AI avoidance summaries and tips
tasks.description: Add Claude Sonnet 4.6 integration to generate 'what this route avoids' summaries and contextual safety tips with prompt caching
tasks.details: Implemented in backend/services/ai_narrator.py. Uses claude-sonnet-4-6 with cache_control on system prompt, 8s timeout with graceful fallback to static tips. Confirmed ai_status: 'ok' in Railway production.
tasks.testStrategy: Test with real route data and verify Claude returns valid JSON with avoidance summary and tips. Verify prompt caching reduces latency on repeat calls. Test timeout fallback by simulating slow API response.

tasks.title: Update backend /routes endpoint to return safest route with AI summary
tasks.description: Refactor /routes endpoint to integrate route scoring, selection, and AI tip generation matching PRD API spec
tasks.details: Updated backend/main.py /routes endpoint: adds departure_time param, calls select_safest_route, then generate_route_narrative. Returns {route, all_routes, safety_score, avoids, tips, ai_status, mode, departure_time}. Also added GET /tips endpoint for tip regeneration.
tasks.testStrategy: Test with various origin/destination/mode/time combinations. Verify safest route is selected. Confirm AI summary and tips are returned. Test with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset (should fallback).

tasks.title: Build frontend route input form with time picker and mode selector
tasks.description: Update frontend to collect origin, destination, departure time (default now), and mode (cycling/walking) with proper validation
tasks.details: Implemented in frontend/app/page.tsx: datetime-local picker defaulting to next 15-min boundary, mode toggle, past-time amber warning, hero stat card ('78% of young Amsterdam women feel unsafe cycling at night'), mission statement ('We're changing that — and giving women back the night').
tasks.testStrategy: Test form submission with all combinations of inputs. Verify time defaults to now. Confirm validation prevents empty submissions. Check past-time warning appears. Verify hero stat and mission render.

tasks.title: Build route results display with avoidance summary, tips, and Google Maps handoff
tasks.description: Create UI to display the safest route with map preview, AI avoidance summary, contextual tips, and one-tap Google Maps deep-link
tasks.details: Implemented in frontend/components/RouteResult.tsx: color-coded safety score badge (green/amber/red), Google Maps JS polyline preview, avoidance summary + area chips, numbered tips list, 'Open in Google Maps →' deep link. Accepts tipsOverride + tipsLoading props for Task 34 integration.

tasks.title: Add GET /tips endpoint for dynamic tip regeneration
tasks.description: Create endpoint to regenerate tips without re-routing when user changes time, allowing interactive exploration
tasks.details: Backend GET /tips endpoint added to main.py. Frontend: page.tsx tracks routeTime vs departureTime; shows amber banner when time changes post-route; 'Update tips' button calls fetchTips() from lib/api.ts without re-routing; RouteResult dims avoids/tips with 'updating…' label during fetch.
